basics: Thai baht (THB). Cards work in cities and malls; carry cash for markets, street food and islands. ATMs charge a fixed fee per withdrawal, so take out more at once.
Grab and Bolt for rides in cities; overnight trains and buses between regions; cheap domestic flights; ferries and longtail boats to the islands.

Cool and dry Nov to Feb in most of the country. The Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi, Phi Phi, Lanta) is best Nov to Apr; the Gulf islands (Samui, Tao) are often best Jan to Aug. The north can be smoky in March and April.
Cover shoulders and knees, take shoes off where others do, never point your feet at a Buddha, and don't touch monks if you are a woman.
The monarchy is deeply respected and protected by strict laws: never joke about or criticise the royal family. Stand for the royal anthem in cinemas.
Buy a tourist SIM or eSIM at the airport. Plugs are mostly types A, B, C and O, at 230 V.
Philippine passport holders can visit Thailand visa-free for a limited stay. Check the current allowed length of stay and the Thailand Digital Arrival Card requirement before you fly.

timing.avoid: Apr to May: hottest weeks, often above 35 C. Sep to Oct: heaviest rain and some street flooding.
timing.note: Songkran water fights in mid April; Loy Krathong lanterns on the river in November.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot with little shade at the ruins. Sep to Oct: river flooding is possible.
timing.note: Day-trippers peak 10 am to 2 pm; stay overnight to see the ruins lit up in the evening.

vibe.line: Sleepy river island of crumbling red-brick temples, best explored slowly by bike.

eat.name: Roti sai mai stalls, U Thong Road
eat.what: Ayutthaya’s candy-floss roti: buy a pack fresh, roll your own.

eat.name: Chao Phrom Market
eat.what: Local market by the river: boat noodles, grilled pork, fruit for pennies.

eat.name: Malakor
eat.what: Thai classics in a wooden house facing Wat Ratchaburana; great after temple hopping.

do.name: Cycle the island
do.what: Temples are flat and close together; a bike is cheaper and freer than a tuk-tuk.

do.name: Sunset longtail around the island
do.what: Boat circles past riverside temples as the light turns gold.

do.name: Bang Pa-In Palace
do.what: Royal summer palace with lakes and pavilions, 20 minutes south.

night.name: Hua Ro night market
night.what: Night market: cheap noodles, grilled skewers, Thai families out for dinner.

night.name: Lit-up Wat Mahathat
night.what: Quiet stroll: some ruins are floodlit after dark, free to view from outside.

night.name: Soi Farang bars, Naresuan Road
night.what: Chill backpacker bars, cheap Leo and pool tables; small but friendly.

know: Rent a bike for 50 to 100 baht a day; tuk-tuk temple tours run about 200 to 300 baht per hour.
The ordinary train from Bangkok costs around 15 to 20 baht in third class and beats tour vans.
Start by 8 am: by noon the brick ruins radiate heat and day-trip coaches roll in from Bangkok.

cities.name: Kanchanaburi
cities.getAround: Bus 8170 runs from town to Erawan for about 50 to 60 baht each way, about 1.5 hours. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day; songthaews and motorbike taxis cover short hops for 30 to 60 baht.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: hot, and the falls run lower. Sep to Oct: muddy trails and murkier pools.
timing.note: River Kwai Bridge Week in late Nov to early Dec brings a light and sound show and big crowds.

vibe.line: River rafthouses, jungle waterfalls and sobering war history, all in slow motion.

eat.name: Saeng Chuto Road stalls
eat.what: Pad krapao and khao man gai for office-worker prices.

eat.name: Kanchanaburi night market by the station
eat.what: Grilled fish, som tam and desserts; locals outnumber tourists.

eat.name: Keeree Tara
eat.what: Riverside terrace near the bridge: river fish, spicy salads, sunset views.

do.name: Death Railway train to Nam Tok
do.what: Creaky train over the Wang Pho wooden viaduct, cliffs on one side.

do.name: Hellfire Pass memorial walk
do.what: Moving trail through the rock cutting; museum is excellent, entry by donation.

do.name: Kayak or bamboo raft the River Kwai
do.what: Lazy paddle past rafthouses and limestone hills.

night.name: Mae Nam Khwae Road bars
night.what: Chill bars and live acoustic sets along the backpacker strip.

night.name: River Kwai Bridge at dusk
night.what: Sunset spot: walk the bridge as lamps come on, then grab street snacks.

know: Stay on Mae Nam Khwae Road: rafthouse rooms run about 400 to 900 baht, scooters 200 to 250 a day.
Public bus to Erawan Falls costs about 50 to 60 baht; check the last return, usually mid-afternoon.
Foreigners pay 100 baht for the Death Railway; sit on the river side for the viaduct views.

cities.name: Sukhothai
cities.getAround: Blue songthaews run between New Sukhothai and the old city for about 30 to 40 baht, 30 minutes. Bicycles at the park gates rent for about 30 to 50 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot for cycling the ruins. Aug to Oct: heavy rain.
timing.note: Loy Krathong (November) is celebrated here with a week of lights and lanterns: book rooms early.

vibe.line: Calm, golden and green: lotus ponds, giant Buddhas and early-morning bike rides.

eat.name: Noodle stalls by the Old City gate
eat.what: Sukhothai noodles: sweet-sour pork broth, peanuts, green beans.

eat.name: New Town night market
eat.what: Locals’ dinner: grilled chicken, sticky rice, fruit shakes.

eat.name: Jay Hae
eat.what: Famous Sukhothai noodle shop; order the dry version and a coconut jelly.

do.name: Dawn bike ride to the west zone
do.what: Empty forest temples and a hilltop Buddha before the heat.

do.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
do.what: Sukhothai’s quieter twin, an hour north; often you have it to yourself.

do.name: Sangkhalok Museum
do.what: Small private museum of old Sukhothai ceramics; cool break from the sun.

night.name: Chopper Bar, New Town
night.what: Chill rooftop bar with live music and cheap Thai plates.

night.name: Old City sunset by the ponds
night.what: Quiet sunset spot: ruins reflected in lotus ponds, then fireflies and frogs.

know: Sleep in the Old City, not New Town, so you can cycle the ruins at 6:30 am.
Blue songthaews link New Town and the Old City for about 30 baht; last ones leave late afternoon.
Loy Krathong here is Thailand’s most famous; rooms double in price, so book weeks ahead.

cities.name: Chiang Mai
cities.getAround: Red songthaews are shared taxis: about 30 to 50 baht within town if you share, more to go further. Grab or Bolt is 60 to 200 baht across town; scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: burning season smoke and haze, poor air quality. Jun to Sep: rainy.
timing.note: Yi Peng lanterns and Loy Krathong in November draw huge crowds; Songkran in April is the wettest party in the country.

vibe.line: Laid-back mountain city of cafes, khao soi, temples and the cheapest massages around.

eat.name: Chang Phueak Gate night stalls
eat.what: Braised pork leg on rice from the cowboy-hat lady, plus smoothies.

eat.name: Warorot Market
eat.what: Northern snacks: sai oua sausage, nam prik dips, crispy pork to take away.

eat.name: Huen Phen
eat.what: Northern Thai in an antique-filled house: khao soi, gaeng hang lay.

do.name: Cooking class with market tour
do.what: Half-day class, five dishes, farm or market visit; most include pickup.

do.name: Sticky Waterfall (Bua Tong)
do.what: Climb up a waterfall with grippy limestone; free and fun.

do.name: Wat Umong forest temple
do.what: Tunnel temple in the woods, quiet monks, feed the fish.

night.name: Sunday Walking Street
night.what: Huge night market down Ratchadamnoen: crafts, food, temple-yard dining.

night.name: North Gate Jazz Co-op
night.what: Live music: packed jam sessions spilling onto the street.

night.name: Nimman Soi 11 and Think Park
night.what: Party-lite: student bars, craft beer, small clubs nearby.

know: Red songthaews are shared: say your stop, pay about 30 to 40 baht in town; agree before boarding.
February to April is smoke season; check AQI and plan Pai or the islands instead if it’s bad.
Local massage shops charge about 200 to 300 baht an hour, half of Bangkok spa prices.

cities.name: Pai
cities.getAround: Pai is small: walk the town, then rent a scooter (150 to 250 baht a day) for canyon, falls and hot springs. Without a licence and experience, hire a local driver or join a sightseeing tour (about 300 to 500 baht).

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoky and hazy. Jul to Sep: slippery mountain road and landslide risk.
timing.note: Dec to Jan weekends fill with Thai holidaymakers; book ahead and pack a warm layer for nights near 10 C.

vibe.line: Hippie mountain valley: scooters, sunsets, hot springs and bars that start late.

eat.name: Pai Walking Street stalls
eat.what: Khao soi, lasagne, mango sticky rice, anything on a stick.

eat.name: Pai Morning Market
eat.what: Local breakfast: jok rice porridge, patongo, fresh soy milk.

eat.name: Om Garden Cafe
eat.what: Healthy brunch bowls and smoothies in a leafy garden.

do.name: Pai Canyon at sunset
do.what: Narrow ridges and drop-offs; go 5 pm, wear grippy shoes.

do.name: Tha Pai Hot Springs
do.what: Steamy natural pools in the forest; foreigners pay national park fee.

do.name: Boon Ko Ku So bamboo bridge
do.what: Long bamboo walkway over rice fields, best early with mist.

night.name: Walking Street
night.what: Night market: food carts, buskers, cheap souvenirs every evening.

night.name: Edible Jazz
night.what: Chill live acoustic and jazz in a garden, cushions on the floor.

night.name: Don’t Cry Bar
night.what: Party: riverside late-night bar where everyone ends up.

know: Only ride a scooter if you already can; the 762-curve road and gravel sends many tourists to Pai hospital.
Morning minivans from Chiang Mai cost about 200 to 250 baht; sit up front and skip a big breakfast.
December and January nights drop near 10 C; bring a fleece, bungalows rarely have heating.

cities.name: Chiang Rai
cities.getAround: Local buses run from the old bus terminal to the White Temple for about 20 to 30 baht. Grab works in town; a driver for a full temples day is roughly 1,200 to 1,800 baht per car.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoke and haze across the north. Jul to Sep: rainy season.
timing.note: Flower festival season runs Dec to Jan; the night bazaar is busiest at weekends.

vibe.line: Small, easygoing city with wild modern temples and tea hills next door.

eat.name: Saturday Walking Street, Thanalai Road
eat.what: Street food mile: sai oua, khanom krok, northern dips.

eat.name: Night Bazaar food court
eat.what: Hotpot, grilled fish and cheap beer by the live stage.

eat.name: Larb Lung Eed
eat.what: Northern-style larb with herbs and crispy pork skin; a local favourite.

do.name: Blue Temple (Wat Rong Suea Ten)
do.what: Electric-blue interior and white Buddha; free, less crowded than White Temple.

do.name: Baan Dam (Black House)
do.what: Dark, strange art compound of wooden halls and bones.

do.name: Singha Park
do.what: Cycle tea fields and lakes; flat, green, great for a slow afternoon.

night.name: Clock Tower light show
night.what: Golden tower lights up with music at 7, 8 and 9 pm; free.

night.name: Night Bazaar live stage
night.what: Chill: folk singers, cheap beer, families sharing hotpot.

know: Hit the White Temple at opening, then the Blue Temple; Grab between them is cheap and quick.
Green Bus from Chiang Mai is about 180 to 300 baht, depending on class, and very comfortable.
The Golden Triangle is underwhelming on rushed tours; spend that day at Doi Mae Salong tea village instead.

cities.name: Khao Sok
cities.getAround: Khlong Sok village is walkable to the park gate. Cheow Lan Lake is about an hour away: join a tour (day trip around 1,500 to 2,500 baht) or hire a longtail at the dam for a few thousand baht per boat.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: rainy, leeches on trails and some trails close. Oct to Nov is the wettest.
timing.note: Floating raft houses on the lake book out on Thai holidays; one to two nights is the sweet spot.

vibe.line: Ancient rainforest, misty limestone and floating lake huts with zero nightlife.

eat.name: Main road roti and fruit stalls
eat.what: Banana roti and shakes after a jungle walk.

eat.name: Phanom town market
eat.what: Real local market 20 minutes away: curries in bags, cheap fruit.

eat.name: Pawn’s Restaurant
eat.what: Friendly family kitchen; massaman and green curry done right.

do.name: Guided night jungle walk
do.what: Spot spiders, frogs, sleeping birds and maybe a tarantula.

do.name: Sok River tubing or canoe
do.what: Float under limestone cliffs, watch for monkeys.

do.name: Waterfall trail in the park
do.what: Easy self-guided walk to falls and swimming holes.

night.name: Stargazing from a lake raft house
night.what: Quiet: no lights, jungle sounds, millions of stars.

night.name: Riverside bungalow bars
night.what: Chill: a cold Chang by the river and early bed.

know: Book the Cheow Lan lake overnight in the village; Phuket and Krabi agents charge far more for the same raft.
After rain the trails are leech city; leech socks in the village cost about 100 to 150 baht.
There are a few ATMs on the main road, but they can run dry; arrive with enough cash.

cities.name: Krabi (Ao Nang and Railay)
cities.getAround: Longtails from Ao Nang to Railay cost about 100 to 150 baht one way and leave when full. Songthaews link Ao Nang and Krabi Town for about 60 to 80 baht; scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: southwest monsoon, rough seas, fewer boats and some island trips cancelled.
timing.note: Christmas to mid January is the priciest stretch; book Railay rooms early.

vibe.line: Jaw-dropping limestone cliffs, longtail boats, climbers by day and fire shows by night.

eat.name: Krabi Town Night Market (Chao Fah)
eat.what: Weekend market: grilled squid, pad thai, half Ao Nang prices.

eat.name: Ao Nang Landmark Night Market
eat.what: Easy food court with seafood, curries and live music.

eat.name: Krua Thara
eat.what: Locals’ seafood spot: pick your fish, steamed with lime and chilli.

do.name: Rock climbing in Railay
do.what: Half day with a guide, no experience needed; world-class cliffs.

do.name: Kayak Ao Thalane
do.what: Paddle through mangroves and limestone canyons, quiet and green.

do.name: Hong Islands by longtail
do.what: Lagoon, white sand, snorkelling; go early to beat the speedboats.

night.name: Last Bar, Railay East
night.what: Party: fire show, buckets and Thai DJ under the cliffs.

night.name: Ao Nang Centre Point bars
night.what: Party: reggae and cocktail bars, loud till late.

night.name: Railay West sunset
night.what: Chill sunset spot: sand, cliffs and a beer from the stall.

know: Longtails from Ao Nang to Railay cost about 100 to 150 baht per person and leave when full.
Eat in Krabi Town on Friday to Sunday nights; same dishes as Ao Nang at roughly half price.
In rainy months, Railay boats can switch to Ao Nam Mao pier; ask at the beach ticket booth.

cities.name: Koh Phi Phi
cities.getAround: No roads: you walk. Longtails to beaches and viewpoints cost about 100 to 300 baht per person; a half-day longtail charter is roughly 1,500 to 3,000 baht per boat.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: rough seas, and Maya Bay closes every year for about two months (Aug to Sep).
timing.note: The island is loud at night near Tonsai and Loh Dalum; pick Long Beach or the north for quiet.

vibe.line: Turquoise bays by day, buckets and fire dancers on the sand by night.

eat.name: Roti carts in Tonsai Village
eat.what: Banana-Nutella roti at midnight, the island’s unofficial dessert.

eat.name: Tonsai local food market
eat.what: Cheap curries and fried rice near the pier, packed with workers.

eat.name: Papaya Restaurant
eat.what: Spicy, honest Thai food; the green curry and som tam are favourites.

do.name: Dawn longtail to Maya Bay and Pileh
do.what: Beat the speedboats; Maya Bay has a separate national park fee.

do.name: Bamboo Island trip
do.what: White sand and clear shallow water for snorkelling.

do.name: Kayak to Monkey Beach
do.what: Paddle round the headland, snorkel; keep food hidden from monkeys.

night.name: Loh Dalum beach bars
night.what: Party: fire shows, buckets, beach dance floor till late.

night.name: Reggae Bar
night.what: Party: drunk-tourist Muay Thai bouts and cheap drinks.

know: Buckets cost 250 to 450 baht on the beach; a 7-Eleven beer beforehand saves plenty.
Want sleep? Stay at the east end or Long Beach; Loh Dalum parties run until about 2 am.
Hire a private longtail at sunrise; split among friends it often costs less than a crowded speedboat tour.

cities.name: Phuket
cities.getAround: Smart Bus and pink songthaews run between Phuket Town and the main beaches for about 50 to 100 baht. Grab is often 300 to 600 baht to a beach; scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: monsoon seas, red flags on west beaches and strong rip currents.
timing.note: The Vegetarian Festival (around Sep to Oct) fills Phuket Town with processions and meat-free street food.

vibe.line: Big island with colourful Sino-Portuguese old town, wild Patong nights and sunset capes.

eat.name: Lock Tien food court, Old Town
eat.what: Old-school stalls: Hokkien noodles, popiah, oyster omelette.

eat.name: Chillva Market
eat.what: Hip night market: grilled seafood, craft beer, container shops.

eat.name: One Chun
eat.what: Phuket-style crab curry and moo hong in a vintage shophouse.

do.name: Promthep Cape sunset
do.what: Phuket’s classic sunset, free; arrive early for a spot.

do.name: Big Buddha
do.what: Huge marble Buddha with island-wide views; cover knees and shoulders.

do.name: Phang Nga Bay day trip
do.what: Sea caves and limestone towers by boat and canoe.

night.name: Bangla Road, Patong
night.what: Full party: clubs, neon and touts; drinks cost bar prices.

night.name: Lard Yai Sunday Walking Street
night.what: Night market along Thalang Road, food and local crafts.

night.name: Timber Hut
night.what: Live music: Thai cover bands and a local crowd in Old Town.

know: Walk away from beach taxi stands and book Grab or Bolt; fares are often far lower.
The orange Smart Bus runs airport to Patong and Rawai for about 100 baht, versus 600 to 800 by taxi.
Stay in Old Town or Kata, not Patong, unless partying; food and rooms cost noticeably less.

cities.name: Koh Lanta
cities.getAround: Sidecar tuk-tuks cost about 100 to 400 baht depending on distance. Most visitors rent a scooter (200 to 300 baht a day) to roam the long west coast.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: many resorts and restaurants close, ferries are reduced and seas are rough.
timing.note: Lanta Lanta Festival in the Old Town in March celebrates the island's mix of cultures.

vibe.line: Long quiet beaches, hammocks and sunsets; the island where people slow right down.

eat.name: Saladan roti and som tam stalls
eat.what: Cheap snacks by the pier: roti, papaya salad, grilled chicken.

eat.name: Saladan market
eat.what: Local fruit, curries and fried snacks, cheaper than beach restaurants.

eat.name: Old Town stilt restaurants
eat.what: Seafood over the water on the quiet east coast.

do.name: Koh Rok snorkel trip
do.what: Best water around Lanta: reef fish and powder sand.

do.name: Scooter loop to Old Town
do.what: Ride the coast road to the Chinese-Muslim fishing village.

do.name: Lanta Animal Welfare
do.what: Visit or walk shelter dogs; free, donations welcome.

night.name: Long Beach sunset bars
night.what: Chill: bean bags on sand, fire twirlers, cheap cocktails.

night.name: Klong Nin beach bars
night.what: Chill: quiet reggae bars and sunset over the water.

know: May to October, many places close and boats shrink; prices fall but check your resort stays open.
Rent a scooter from your bungalow for about 250 baht a day; check brakes before the hilly south.
Lanta’s ATMs cluster in Saladan and Long Beach; withdraw there before heading south.

cities.name: Koh Samui
cities.getAround: Shared songthaews run round the ring road for about 50 to 150 baht. Taxis and Grab are pricey (300 to 700 baht across the island); scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Oct to Dec: the Gulf monsoon brings the heaviest rain and choppy ferry crossings.
timing.note: Fisherman's Village Walking Street runs Friday evenings; Full Moon parties on Koh Phangan fill Samui ferries.

vibe.line: Palm-lined beaches, beach clubs and villas; easy, polished island comfort.

eat.name: Lamai food court and night market
eat.what: Pad thai, BBQ skewers and shakes, island-cheap.

eat.name: Hua Thanon market
eat.what: Muslim fishing-village market: curries, roti, fresh fish.

eat.name: Krua Bophut
eat.what: Seafront Thai in Fisherman’s Village; book a sunset table.

do.name: Koh Tan and Koh Madsum by longtail
do.what: Quiet snorkelling islands off the south coast.

do.name: Na Muang Waterfall
do.what: Swim under falls in the jungle; free lower tier.

do.name: Secret Buddha Garden
do.what: Hilltop sculpture garden; 4x4 or confident scooter only.

night.name: Ark Bar Beach Club, Chaweng
night.what: Party: DJs on the sand, fire show, from afternoon till late.

night.name: Fisherman’s Village Walking Street
night.what: Friday night market: food, crafts, live music.

night.name: Coco Tam’s, Bophut
night.what: Chill: bean bags, fire show and cocktails on the beach.

know: Samui taxis rarely use meters; Grab or Bolt is usually much cheaper. Book from your lobby.
Songthaews run fixed routes on the ring road, roughly 50 to 100 baht by day, more after dark.
October to December is Samui’s rainy season, opposite the Andaman coast; November is often the wettest.

cities.name: Koh Tao
cities.getAround: Shared taxi pickups cost about 100 to 300 baht per person depending on the bay. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day, but the dirt roads are steep, so walk or take taxis if unsure.

timing.avoid: Oct to Dec: monsoon swell, ferry cancellations and poor visibility for diving.
timing.note: Whale shark sightings peak around Mar to May and Sep; diving is good most of the year outside the monsoon.

vibe.line: Tiny dive island: clear bays, scooter tracks and Sairee’s barefoot bar scene.

eat.name: Sairee pad thai and roti carts
eat.what: Late cheap eats after diving or a night out.

eat.name: Mae Haad night food stalls
eat.what: Local dinners by the pier: noodles, grilled meat, fruit.

eat.name: Su Chili
eat.what: Spicy, generous Thai plates; a diver favourite in Sairee.

do.name: Open Water dive course
do.what: One of the world’s cheapest; 3 to 4 days, often with a room deal.

do.name: Snorkel Shark Bay
do.what: Swim off the beach; black-tip reef sharks in the mornings.

do.name: Round-island longtail snorkel trip
do.what: Hits several bays plus Koh Nang Yuan in one day.

night.name: Lotus Bar, Sairee
night.what: Party: fire shows and beach dancing, especially Wednesdays and weekends.

night.name: Fizz Beach Lounge
night.what: Chill: bean bags, sunset cocktails, soft music.

night.name: Sairee Beach sunset
night.what: Free sunset spot; grab a 7-Eleven beer and sit on the sand.

know: Dive schools give cheap or free rooms during courses; ask before booking a room yourself.
Photograph your rental scooter before riding; some shops charge for old scratches on return.
Seas get rough November to December; take seasickness pills before the catamaran from Samui or Chumphon.

Vans leave from Mo Chit area when full.
Taxi or Grab price per car, split it between up to 3 or 4 people.

From Mo Chit or the Southern Bus Terminal, frequent through the day.
Government buses from the Southern Bus Terminal.
Win Tour and others from Mo Chit; first class about 430, VIP about 500 baht.
Train to Phitsanulok, then a local bus to Sukhothai for about 50 to 70 baht.
Bangkok Airways flies to Sukhothai airport, about 30 km from town.
Many daily flights from Don Mueang and Suvarnabhumi; book a few weeks ahead for the low end.
Second class berth (lower costs more) from Krung Thep Aphiwat; sells out weeks ahead in high season.
First class two-berth cabin on the special express.
Overnight VIP buses from Mo Chit.
Buses heading north stop on the Asian Highway outside Ayutthaya.
Train to Phitsanulok, then a local bus to Sukhothai.
Northern trains stop at Ayutthaya; book the same way as from Bangkok.
Overnight buses pass Ayutthaya; booking from Bangkok is easier.
Several daily buses to Chiang Mai Arcade terminal.
About 220 baht at the Arcade terminal counter, more online with hotel pickup. Hundreds of bends: take a pill.
Private car or van per vehicle, with stops on the way.
Green Bus from Arcade terminal about 15 times a day; VIP class is worth it.
Private driver per car, can stop at the White Temple on the way.
Usually via Chiang Mai: van to Arcade terminal, then a Green Bus to Chiang Rai.
Several low-cost flights daily to Krabi airport, 30 to 40 min from Ao Nang.
Overnight government bus from the Southern Bus Terminal or Mo Chit.
Overnight train to Surat Thani, then a bus or van to Krabi.

Overnight buses from the Southern Bus Terminal.

Lomprayah or similar joint ticket: overnight coach then catamaran.

Lomprayah joint ticket via Chumphon, coach plus high-speed catamaran.
Overnight train to Chumphon, then a morning ferry to Mae Haad.
Fly to Chumphon or Surat Thani, then a joint boat ticket.
Overnight train to Surat Thani, then a van to Khlong Sok.
Overnight bus to Surat Thani or direct joint tickets to Khao Sok.
Fly to Surat Thani, then a shared van (about 150 to 300 baht).

Daily direct low-cost flights.
Bangkok Airways direct when scheduled; otherwise via Bangkok.
Big boats from Rassada pier; fares rose by up to 200 baht in April 2026 with fuel costs.
Faster, bumpier, often with hotel pickup included.
From Klong Jilad pier in Krabi Town or Nopparat Thara near Ao Nang.
From Ao Nang; book a day ahead in high season.
Shared van with two short car ferries, hotel pickup.
From Ao Nang, high season only (about Nov to Apr).
Daily big boat from Tonsai pier to Saladan.

Door to door vans to Ao Nang or Krabi Town.
Government buses from Phuket Bus Terminal 2.
Rassada pier to Ao Nang, high season; some go via Phi Phi.
Surat Thani buses from Phuket Terminal 2, ask to stop at Khao Sok.
Shared van with hotel pickup.
Shared vans from Ao Nang and Krabi Town, usually morning departures.
Van to Donsak pier, then ferry; guesthouses sell joint tickets.
Lomprayah high-speed catamaran (about 700 baht) from Maenam, Nathon or Bangrak; via Koh Phangan.
Slower Seatran or Songserm boats, steadier in swell.
Van to Donsak pier, then a car ferry; joint tickets from Ao Nang.
Bangkok Airways direct.
Bus or van to Donsak pier, then a ferry.
High season boats via Phi Phi.

Overnight VIP buses to Mo Chit.

wishIKnew.title: Buy your beer at 7-Eleven
wishIKnew.tip: 7-Eleven: Leo 490 ml about 53 baht, Chang 53 to 55, Singha 56. Bars charge 80 to 150, rooftops 300 plus. A SangSom flask is roughly 150 to 250.

wishIKnew.title: Alcohol sells 11 am to midnight
wishIKnew.tip: Since late May 2026, shops and restaurants sell 11:00 to midnight; the old 2 to 5 pm ban is gone. No sales on Buddhist holy days.

wishIKnew.title: After-hours drinking can be fined
wishIKnew.tip: Since Nov 2025, customers caught drinking outside legal hours at unlicensed places risk fines up to 10,000 baht. Licensed clubs in nightlife zones can serve later.

wishIKnew.title: Withdraw big, withdraw rarely
wishIKnew.tip: Foreign cards pay about 220 to 350 baht per ATM withdrawal. Take 20,000 to 30,000 at once, decline the conversion, try AEON ATMs (about 150).

wishIKnew.title: Change money at SuperRich
wishIKnew.tip: Skip arrival-hall booths. SuperRich (orange) in Suvarnabhumi basement, by the Rail Link, or in town pays noticeably better. Clean, unmarked USD notes get the best rate.

wishIKnew.title: Rail Link beats the taxi
wishIKnew.tip: Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai: 45 baht, about 26 minutes. A taxi runs roughly 300 to 500 with the 50 baht airport fee, tolls and traffic.

wishIKnew.title: Street food costs a third
wishIKnew.tip: Pad krapao or noodles cost 50 to 80 baht at stalls, 150 to 300 in tourist restaurants. Follow office workers at lunch for the best spots.

wishIKnew.title: 7-Eleven is your safety net
wishIKnew.tip: Ham and cheese toastie 30 to 45 baht, microwave meals 40 to 70, staff heat them free. Also cheap sunscreen, medicine, SIM top-ups.

wishIKnew.title: Grab first, tuk-tuk for fun
wishIKnew.tip: Grab or Bolt short city hops run about 60 to 150 baht; tuk-tuks quote 150 to 300. Ride one once for the photo, agree the price first.

wishIKnew.title: Shared songthaew, not charter
wishIKnew.tip: Chiang Mai red trucks cost about 30 to 40 baht shared in town. If the driver says charter or names 150 plus, it’s private. Wave the next.

wishIKnew.title: Grand Palace: dress and scam
wishIKnew.tip: “Palace closed today” is a scam leading to gem shops; walk to the gate yourself. Cover shoulders and knees; elephant pants cost 100 to 150 at markets.

wishIKnew.title: Massage and laundry are cheap
wishIKnew.tip: Thai massage: 200 to 350 baht an hour in local shops, 800 plus in spas. Laundry by weight: 40 to 100 baht a kilo, islands up to 150.

wishIKnew.title: Get a tourist SIM or eSIM
wishIKnew.tip: AIS, True or dtac tourist SIMs cost about 299 to 449 baht for 8 days at airport counters; carrier eSIMs are similar. Bring your passport.

wishIKnew.title: Expect dual pricing
wishIKnew.tip: National parks charge foreigners 200 to 500 baht versus about 40 to 100 for Thais. Budget for it; arguing never works.

wishIKnew.title: Bargain at markets, not malls
wishIKnew.tip: At night markets start near half the first price and smile. Malls, 7-Eleven and food courts are fixed. Blue water machines refill a litre for 1 to 2 baht.

events.name: Sukhothai Loy Krathong and Candle Festival
events.what: The original Loy Krathong: candlelit ruins, fireworks and light and sound shows in the Historical Park.
events.tip: Stay inside the old city so you can walk back late; the light and sound show needs tickets.

events.name: Yi Peng Chiang Saen: Light of Faith on the Mekong
events.what: Lanna lantern nights on the Mekong riverbank at Chiang Saen, quieter than Chiang Mai.
events.tip: Chiang Saen is about 1.5 hours from Chiang Rai town; go by day and stay for dusk.

events.name: Loy Krathong
events.what: Full moon night: everyone floats candlelit krathongs on rivers, lakes and the sea to say thanks.
events.tip: Buy a banana leaf or bread krathong (no foam) from street stalls, about 50 to 100 baht.

events.name: Yi Peng and Loy Krathong, Chiang Mai
events.what: Sky lanterns, glowing old city gates and a krathong parade along the Ping River.
events.tip: Book rooms early; lanterns may only be released at permitted zones, so follow local rules.

events.name: River Kwai Bridge Week and Red Cross Fair
events.what: Nightly light and sound show at the Death Railway bridge, plus a big fair and food stalls.
events.tip: Shows start around 7pm; buy show seats a day ahead and bring mosquito spray.

events.name: Wonderfruit 2026
events.what: Arty, eco minded five day festival of music, talks and wellness at The Fields near Pattaya.
events.tip: About 2 hours from Bangkok; tickets sold only on wonderfruit.co, no refunds or transfers.

events.name: BTS World Tour ARIRANG in Bangkok
events.what: BTS stadium shows at Rajamangala on 3, 5 and 6 December; expect huge crowds around Ramkhamhaeng.
events.tip: Officially sold out; avoid scalpers and take the Airport Rail Link to Ramkhamhaeng.

events.name: Phuket King's Cup Regatta
events.what: Asia's big royal sailing regatta, with yachts racing off Kata and lively shore parties.
events.tip: Watch the starts from Kata Beach or the hill viewpoints; Kata rooms fill fast that week.

events.name: Chiang Mai Design Week 2026
events.what: Citywide design shows, pop up exhibits and makers markets across Chiang Mai's creative districts.
events.tip: Most exhibitions are free; grab the map and cycle between Nimman, Wat Ket and the old city.

events.name: Krabi ReWild Festival
events.what: Eco festival around Krabi's climbing scene: rock climbing, yoga and live music.
events.tip: Dates follow last year's pattern; check before booking and pack climbing shoes if you have them.

events.name: King Bhumibol Memorial Day (Father's Day)
events.what: National holiday honouring the late King Rama IX; yellow flags and ceremonies at government sites.
events.tip: Banks and offices close; tourist spots stay open but Bangkok's Sanam Luang area gets busy.

events.name: Tomorrowland Thailand
events.what: Tomorrowland's first Asian outdoor edition at Wisdom Valley, Pattaya: giant stages, world class DJs.
events.tip: About 2 hours from Bangkok, no camping; 3 day passes sold out fast, check official resale.

events.name: EDC Thailand (December edition)
events.what: Insomniac's neon EDM carnival at Rhythm Park, Laguna Phuket, three nights of big room bass.
events.tip: Strictly 20 plus, bring your passport; hotel bundles include shuttles from Patong and Laguna.

events.name: Chiang Rai Flower Festival
events.what: Cool season blooms, flower tunnels and evening music in Chiang Rai's riverside park.
events.tip: Go late afternoon for golden light; dates follow last season, so confirm with TAT Chiang Rai.

events.name: Bangkok New Year Countdown
events.what: Free riverside fireworks at ICONSIAM plus concerts and drones at CentralWorld and One Bangkok.
events.tip: Take the BTS or a boat early, trains get packed after 10pm; bring water and patience.

events.name: Ao Nang New Year Countdown
events.what: Beach countdown at Ao Nang and Noppharat Thara with DJs, food stalls and midnight fireworks.
events.tip: Book longtail transfers back from Railay before dusk; boats stop early that night.

events.name: New Year's Day holiday
events.what: Nationwide New Year holiday; Thais travel home, so buses, trains and flights fill up.
events.tip: Book transport and island ferries at least two weeks ahead; prices spike over the break.

events.name: Stray Kids World Tour RUN IT in Bangkok
events.what: K pop arena shows at IMPACT Arena, Muang Thong Thani, on Bangkok's northern edge.
events.tip: Listed by aggregators only; confirm on the promoter's page and allow an hour by taxi from central Bangkok.

events.name: Bo Sang Umbrella Festival
events.what: Craft village fair of hand painted paper umbrellas, parades and a Miss Bo Sang contest on bicycles.
events.tip: Bo Sang is a short songthaew ride east of Chiang Mai; get a free umbrella sketch on your bag.

events.name: Chiang Mai Flower Festival (50th)
events.what: Flower covered floats parade from Nawarat Bridge to Suan Buak Haad park; garden displays all weekend.
events.tip: Grab a curbside spot on Saturday morning before 8am; dates are announced in January.

events.name: Chinese New Year in Yaowarat
events.what: Bangkok's Chinatown turns red and gold with lion dances, lanterns and street food crowds.
events.tip: Go early evening by MRT to Wat Mangkon; some Chinese owned shops close for a few days.

events.name: Ayutthaya World Heritage Fair
events.what: Ten nights of light and sound shows, period costume and old Siam food stalls in the Historical Park.
events.tip: The 2026 fair moved to February; confirm 2027 dates before planning. Rent Thai costume for photos.

events.name: Makha Bucha Day
events.what: Buddhist holy day: candlelit wian tian walks around temples; substitute holiday on Monday 22nd.
events.tip: Alcohol sales are banned nationwide on the day and many bars close; plan a temple visit instead.

events.name: Laanta Lanta Festival
events.what: Three day Old Town fest of Chao Leh sea gypsy culture, reggae, food and handicrafts.
events.tip: 2026 ran 27 to 29 March; 2027 dates not yet out, watch Krabi tourism pages.

events.name: Songkran (Thai New Year)
events.what: Nationwide water fight and family homecoming; temples bathe Buddha images, streets become splash zones.
events.tip: Bag your phone in a dry pouch, book transport early, and expect many shops and offices shut.

events.name: S2O Songkran Music Festival
events.what: Bangkok's soaking EDM party over Songkran with water cannons and big name DJs.
events.tip: 2027 dates and lineup not announced yet; tickets usually sell from January on Eventpop.

events.name: Bruno Mars The Romantic Tour
events.what: Two stadium nights at Rajamangala with DJ Pee.Wee (Anderson .Paak) opening.
events.tip: Promoted by Live Nation Tero; buy only from the official seller and arrive early for security.

events.name: Spotlight Koh Tao
events.what: Island sustainability festival on Sairee: coral planting, eco market and beach music.
events.tip: Estimated from 2026's 1 to 3 May; join a reef clean up dive for a cheap fun dive.

events.name: Visakha Bucha Day
events.what: Holiest Buddhist day, marking the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death; candle processions at night.
events.tip: No alcohol sold nationwide and many bars close; dress modestly if joining temple walks.

events.name: Samui Regatta (24th)
events.what: Relaxed yacht racing week off Samui's north coast with sunset regatta parties.
events.tip: Dates announced at the 2026 closing; watch from Bophut or Choeng Mon beaches.

events.name: Asanha Bucha and Khao Phansa
events.what: Start of Buddhist Lent; candle festivals, especially big in Ubon, and temple offerings everywhere.
events.tip: Two dry days: no alcohol sales nationwide on both; Monday 19th is a public holiday.

events.name: King Vajiralongkorn's Birthday
events.what: National holiday with royal portraits, yellow decor and evening ceremonies.
events.tip: Government offices and banks close; dress respectfully near royal ceremonies.

events.name: Queen Mother's Birthday (Mother's Day)
events.what: National holiday honouring Queen Sirikit; blue decor, jasmine garlands and family outings.
events.tip: Long weekend crowds at beach towns near Bangkok; book ahead.

events.name: Phuket Vegetarian Festival
events.what: Nine days of Taoist rites in Phuket Town: firecracker processions, face piercing devotees, meat free food.
events.tip: Wear white, bring earplugs, and eat at the yellow flag stalls; processions start at dawn.

events.name: Sukhothai Loy Krathong and Candle Festival
events.what: Ten nights of candles, fireworks and shows among Sukhothai's ruins, ending on Loy Krathong night.
events.tip: Estimated from the usual pattern; book rooms by September once dates are out.

events.name: Yi Peng and Loy Krathong, Chiang Mai
events.what: Lantern nights, river krathongs and the Ping River parade, the north's most magical week.
events.tip: Estimated around the 14 November full moon; hotels fill months ahead.

events.name: Loy Krathong
events.what: Full moon of the twelfth lunar month: candlelit krathongs float on every river and beach.
events.tip: Most sources say 14 November; a few say the 13th, so confirm in early 2027.

events.name: Full Moon Party, Koh Phangan
events.what: Haad Rin beach rave near Samui and Koh Tao: neon paint, buckets, fire skipping, sunrise.
events.tip: Entry about 100 to 200 baht; book the late boat back or a room, they sell out weeks ahead.

events.name: Rajadamnern World Series Muay Thai
events.what: Bangkok's oldest stadium, Saturday showcase card with fast, modern style Muay Thai.
events.tip: Buy at the stadium box office to skip reseller markups; second class seats feel the most local.

events.name: ONE Lumpinee Muay Thai
events.what: Friday fight night at Lumpinee, 7:30 to 11:30pm, slick TV production and loud crowds.
events.tip: Buy on ThaiTicketMajor at face value; MRT to Bang Khen area then a short taxi.

events.name: Sunday Walking Street (Tha Phae to Wat Phra Singh)
events.what: Ratchadamnoen Road closes for a huge night market of crafts, buskers and northern snacks.
events.tip: Arrive around 5pm before the crush; try khao soi and sai ua sausage from temple courtyards.

events.name: Chiang Rai Saturday Walking Street
events.what: Thanalai Road fills with hill tribe crafts, Lanna dancing and cheap street food.
events.tip: Starts around 4 to 6pm; Sunday has a smaller market on San Khong Noi Road.

events.name: Pai Walking Street
events.what: Every evening Pai's main street becomes a backpacker food and art market with live music bars.
events.tip: Busiest 7 to 9pm; bring small notes and try the lasagna and khao soi stalls.

events.name: Fisherman's Village Walking Street, Bophut
events.what: Friday night market in Bophut's old wooden shophouses, 5 to 11pm, food, crafts and beach bars.
events.tip: Parking is hard; take a songthaew or Bolt, and eat seafood on the beach afterwards.

events.name: Lamai Sunday Walking Street
events.what: Lamai's centre turns into a laid back Sunday night market, 5 to 11pm.
events.tip: Cheaper than Bophut; good for souvenirs and grilled seafood.

events.name: Loh Dalum beach fire shows
events.what: Ibiza, Slinky and Stones bars on Loh Dalum: fire dancers, buckets and beach DJs till 2am.
events.tip: Shows run about 9 to 11pm; skip fire limbo and fire skipping after a few buckets.

events.name: Sairee Beach bar nights
events.what: Lotus and Fishbowl fire shows, beer pong and DJs along Sairee from sunset to 2am.
events.tip: Busiest 9pm to 2am; skip big nights before early dives, and walk back with a torch.

events.name: Bangla Road, Patong
events.what: Patong's neon walking street of clubs, bars and loud street touts, wild every night.
events.tip: Agree prices before any show, watch your drinks, and use Grab or Bolt back.
